questions.question: Sound is produced by:
questions.explanation: Sound is produced when an object vibrates — the vibrations travel through a medium as sound waves.

questions.question: Sound travels fastest through:
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest through solids (like steel) because particles are closely packed.

questions.question: What is the unit of loudness of sound?
questions.explanation: Sound loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

questions.question: Can sound travel in vacuum?
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot travel through vacuum.

questions.question: What is pitch of sound?
questions.explanation: Pitch refers to how high or low a sound is, related to the frequency of vibration.

questions.question: A high-pitched sound has:
questions.explanation: High-pitched sounds vibrate at high frequencies (many vibrations per second).

questions.question: What is an echo?
questions.explanation: An echo is a reflection of sound that reaches the listener after bouncing off a surface.

questions.question: What frequency range can humans hear?
questions.explanation: Humans can hear sounds in the range 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.

questions.question: Sounds above 20,000 Hz are called:
questions.explanation: Sounds above 20,000 Hz are called ultrasound. Bats use ultrasound for navigation.

questions.question: Why do we hear our voice differently when recorded?
options: We normally hear our voice through bones + air, recording is air only
Our voice changes when we speak aloud
questions.explanation: We hear our voice through both bone conduction and air. Recordings only capture the air-conducted sound.

questions.question: A guitar string vibrates 440 times per second. Its frequency is:
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in Hertz (Hz). 440 vibrations per second = 440 Hz.

questions.question: Which material absorbs sound best?
questions.explanation: Soft materials like foam absorb sound. Hard surfaces reflect it (causing echoes).

questions.question: Loud sounds above 85 dB can cause:
questions.explanation: Prolonged exposure to sounds above 85 dB can cause permanent hearing damage.

questions.question: A stethoscope allows doctors to:
questions.explanation: A stethoscope conducts and amplifies body sounds (heartbeat, breathing) to the doctor's ears.

questions.question: Thunder is heard after lightning because:
questions.explanation: Light travels at 3×10⁸ m/s while sound travels at ~340 m/s in air. Light reaches us almost instantly; sound takes time.
